answer: Random mutual audits stop identity forgery by making each identity face unrelated reviewers. Each epoch a beacon picks three auditors for every identity; auditors compare its work log against a ferrous registry entry binding one key to one history, so audit rental fails. A grove of clones cannot share one auditor pool, because each clone needs its own three audits and a failed audit slashes a 40-credit bond. Forging 1,000 identities risks 40,000 credits, with loss rising in a spiral as each clone adds its own audit cost, while an honest agent pays one refundable bond.
